chunks.title: AKGEC Digital School
chunks.content: AKGEC established a Digital Studio with high-end video and audio recording facilities to promote quality education and online learning, supporting lecture recording, live streaming of events, and interviews. To give students and the academic community easy access to this digital content, a YouTube channel named 'AKGEC DIGITAL SCHOOL' was created on 8 July 2020. The channel hosts 600+ recorded and uploaded lectures across various engineering subjects, with a cumulative watch time of around 8,200 hours. It has been viewed by almost 138,000+ viewers and has around 20,000+ subscribers. Channel link: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCxs6M6Um-IYd9eD3XUHRlkg/playlists.

chunks.title: Educational Verification
chunks.content: For verification of educational details of AKGEC students, external parties should visit the 'Services' link on the AKTU university website (www.aktu.ac.in). If there is a problem or delay in the University's response, the following process applies: mail the student's final year marksheet and/or degree certificate along with a verification request to the college's registrar email. A reply is sent within three working days of the College. If there is no reply within that window, contact Dr. Shraddha Dixit, Registrar, at mobile 9818391726 between 10 am and 4 pm, except Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays.

chunks.title: Policy and Process for Refund of Caution Money
chunks.content: Caution money and security deposit are refunded after deduction of any dues, only after a student finally leaves the College on completion of their course. Final-year students must fill a clearance form (No Dues Form) and submit it to the Accounts Office before leaving. The Accounts Office processes these forms and distributes caution money cheques at the College Convocation, informing students individually by letter and email. Most cheques are distributed in one go on a single day. Students who miss the Convocation Ceremony may collect their cheque on any other working day during College hours.

chunks.subtopic: Issuance of Certificates for Passout Students
chunks.title: Issuance of Certificates for Passout Students
chunks.content: Documents required for issuance of certificates to passout students: Character Certificate — photocopy of final year marksheet, No Dues certificate from Accounts. Transfer Certificate — photocopy of final year marksheet, photocopy of 10th pass certificate, Rs. 50 processing fee receipt from Accounts, No Dues certificate. Migration Certificate — apply online via the AKTU portal (erp.aktu.ac.in). Degree Certificate — government-issued ID proof of the student, No Dues certificate; in the student's absence, parents/guardians may collect it with their own government ID and an authority letter from the student. Students must collect their T.C. and Character Certificate within one month of applying (online or offline). Late collection within the next month incurs a Rs. 200 fine; certificates not collected within two months are cancelled and must be re-applied for at a combined cost of Rs. 500.

chunks.title: College Awards
chunks.content: AKGEC has received the Diamond Rating by QS I-GAUGE, recognizing academic excellence, innovation, and holistic institutional development. Other notable awards and recognitions include: NABL accreditation (ISO/IEC 17025:2017) for the Measurement & Metrology Centre, developed in collaboration with Zeiss, covering 3D CMM, surface roughness testing, contour measurement, and 3D scanning. A patent for a 3-D Printer developed by Mr. Pradeep Jain, Associate Professor, Mechanical Engineering, under the Research and Industrial Consultancy Centre. AICRA 2020 STEM Award (India STEM College Award) and Best Robolab Setup — third consecutive year AKGEC was honored at the STEM Awards & Summit. AICRA 2019 Award for Excellence and Innovation in Robotics Education (at IIT Delhi). AICRA 2018 Awards for Best Technology Infrastructure of the Year and Best Vocational Robotics Educational Centre. NAFEMS UK 2018 Award for Best Industry Institute Interaction. Dialogue India 2018 Award for Best Private Engineering College in North India. Best LabVIEW Academy Award by National Instruments (2016) — over 600 engineers trained, 204 CLAD and 17 CLD certifications achieved. Best Institution for Innovation Award (2015) from the Entrepreneurship and Skill Development Association. Emerging LabVIEW Academy Award, North India (2014) by National Instruments. Best Institute Award by CMAI (2013). Dialogue India Academia Award 2013 — First Rank among engineering colleges affiliated to Mahamaya Technical University (MTU), Noida. Academic Excellence Award by UPTU for three consecutive years (2008, 2009, 2010), plus several UPTU appreciation letters (2005–2008) and a Best Engineering College Award from the Ghaziabad Management Association (2008).

chunks.title: About IQAC
chunks.content: Per NAAC guidelines, every accredited institution must establish an Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) as a pre-accreditation quality sustenance measure. IQAC works towards continuous quality enhancement and sustenance as an integral part of the institution's system. Its prime task is to develop a system for conscious, consistent, and catalytic improvement in overall institutional performance. AKGEC was first accredited by NAAC in 2015; the NAAC team visited the AKGEC campus from 22–24 January 2015.

chunks.title: Goals and Benefits of IQAC
chunks.content: IQAC's goal is to introduce a consistent plan of action driving institutional progress via strategies for: efficient and timely work processes, academic research and programs, affordable and innovative approaches, use of ICT for modernizing education, best assessment processes for quality maintenance, and ensuring the best infrastructure to achieve institutional goals. Cited benefits of IQAC in the NAAC accreditation process include: clarifying and re-thinking work processes, internalizing a quality culture, improving inter-departmental collaboration, improving overall institutional functioning through transparency, enabling proper documentation, encouraging R&D, ensuring greater transparency via peer verification, promoting project- and service-based learning, encouraging professional development programs, and providing students a globalized ('think locally, act globally') platform.

chunks.title: Functions, Objectives and Tasks of IQAC
chunks.content: IQAC's objectives: develop a system for conscious, consistent, catalytic action to improve academic and administrative performance; promote institutional functioning towards quality enhancement via internalization of quality culture and best practices. Its strategies cover timely/efficient task performance, relevance and quality of academic and research programs, equitable and affordable access to programs, integration of modern teaching methods, credibility of evaluation, adequacy of support structures, and sharing research findings via networking. Key tasks include: quality assurance, accreditation/assessment preparation, continuous improvement, benchmarking against national/international standards, strategic planning, feedback and grievance handling, faculty/staff development, research and innovation support, documentation and reporting, data collection and analysis, best-practice dissemination, stakeholder engagement, resource mobilization, preparing and submitting the AQAR to NAAC annually, mentoring systems, academic/administration/accounts audits, implementation of OBE/NEP, and regulatory compliance. IQAC meets at least once every quarter, with a quorum of two-thirds of total members; agendas, minutes, and Action Taken Reports are documented with official signatures and retained electronically.

chunks.title: Annual Quality Assurance Reports (AQAR) — Archive
chunks.content: AKGEC publishes an Annual Quality Assurance Report (AQAR) each year, submitted to NAAC. Archived reports available: AQAR 2023-2024, 2022-2023, 2021-2022, 2020-2021, 2019-2020, 2018-2019, 2017-2018, 2016-2017, and 2015-2016, each linked from the IQAC page. Additional NAAC-criterion-wise supporting documents (Curricular Aspects, Teaching-Learning and Evaluation, Research/Innovations/Extension, Infrastructure, Student Support, Governance/Leadership/Management, Institutional Values and Best Practices) are published for sessions 2023-24 and 2022-23, including feedback systems, NPTEL certificates, experiential learning reports, ICT tools documentation, internal assessment mechanisms, Ph.D. registration data, audited financial statements, and student satisfaction surveys.
